User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the SyncWatch platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

avatar.description: URL of the user's avatar image.

email.description: The user's email address. (Used for login)

googleId.description: The user's Google ID (Used for Google login)

id.description: Unique identifier for the Room entity.

hostId.description: Reference to User who is the host. (Relationship: User 1:N Room)

contentSourceType.description: Type of content source (YouTube, direct link, uploaded file, screen share).

contentSource.description: The actual content source (URL, file path, etc.).

shareableLink.description: Unique link for others to join the room.

locked.description: Indicates whether the room is locked or not.

hangoutMode.description: Indicates whether the room is in Hangout mode (with voice/video chat) or Watch mode.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description: Represents a chat message within a room.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ChatMessage entity.

userId.description: Reference to User who sent the message. (Relationship: User 1:N ChatMessage)

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the message was sent.

message.description: The text of the chat message.

EmojiReaction.title: EmojiReaction
EmojiReaction.description: Represents an emoji reaction to a chat message.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EmojiReaction entity.

userId.description: Reference to User who reacted. (Relationship: User 1:N EmojiReaction)

emoji.description: The emoji that was used as a reaction.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the reaction was added.

RoomUser.title: RoomUser
RoomUser.description: Represents the association between a User and a Room, including connection status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RoomUser entity.

roomId.description: Reference to Room. (Relationship: Room N:N User)

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User N:N Room)

isConnected.description: Indicates whether the user is currently connected to the room.

isHost.description: Indicates whether the user is the host of the room.

isMuted.description: Indicates whether the user is currently muted in the room.

cameraEnabled.description: Indicates whether the user's camera is enabled in the room.

definition.description: Stores user profiles.  The `userId` parameter is the user's Firebase UID. Used for profile information and authentication.

params.name: userId
params.description: The Firebase UID of the user.

definition.description: Stores room metadata. Includes hostId and content source information.
Stores chat messages for a room. Includes roomId for authorization independence.
Stores emoji reactions to chat messages. Includes messageId and userId.
Stores the association between users and rooms, including connection status and roles. Includes roomId and userId for authorization.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support SyncWatch's features, emphasizing security, scalability, and ease of debugging. It incorporates denormalization for authorization independence and structural segregation for simplified security rules. User data is stored in a dedicated collection. Rooms are stored separately for easy listing and querying. Chat messages, emoji reactions, and room user associations are structured as subcollections to maintain data integrity and optimize queries. The design leverages path-based ownership and membership maps for access control, ensuring secure list operations (QAPs) and atomic operations across the platform.

Authorization Independence is achieved by denormalizing authorization data (e.g., hostId, members) into subcollections. For example, each `ChatMessage` includes the `roomId`, allowing rules to validate the user's access to a room's messages without needing to perform `get()` operations on the parent `Room` document. The RoomUser document contains the `isHost` and `isConnected` flags, allowing rules to easily validate write access based on the user's role in the room.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters) is achieved by segregating data based on access requirements and leveraging denormalization. By storing messages within the `/rooms/{roomId}/messages/{messageId}` subcollection, we can easily secure list operations. The presence of `roomId` within the message allows us to validate user access based on their membership in the room.
